note: Sanctioned Archer compositions. `signature` is the normalized component tree — a node is `[name, ...children]`, matching is containment rather than equality, and anything under four nodes the engine ignores as too generic to check. Archer's parts are flat sibling exports off one import (`DialogPopup`, not `Dialog.Popup`), so a signature is written in those names. Two kinds of entry live here and they do different jobs. **Anatomy entries** record a shape the library *requires* — a Dialog is a root, a trigger, a popup and a title, in every file that has one. They exist so `patterns/unregistered-composite` does not report a component's own mandatory anatomy as house style nobody wrote down; each carries `canonical` set to the root import, so any file actually using the component is skipped before either composite rule sees it, and they therefore never produce a finding. **Judgement entries** record a composite that has a right and a wrong form; those carry `instead_of` and, where the wrong form is a recognisable composite in its own right, `instead_of_signature`. Most do not — the shape reached for by default is usually one control, and a rule that fires on every `Select` is a rule people turn off, which is why reading this file before assembling matters more than the check does. Archer ships no page header, empty state, sidebar or settings drilldown: those entries are here without `canonical` on purpose, so the first project that builds one extracts it and fills that in rather than rebuilding it per screen.

patterns.summary: The parts a Dialog is made of.
patterns.use: Every modal task. Recorded so the required anatomy is not reported as an unregistered composite.

patterns.summary: The parts an AlertDialog is made of.
patterns.use: Destructive or irreversible confirmation.
instead_of: A Dialog with a title, a description and a Cancel/Confirm button pair — AlertDialog already is that, with the dismissal behaviour and button emphasis a destructive action needs
patterns.note: The anti-shape is deliberately prose rather than an `instead_of_signature`: a form dialog also carries a title, a description and two buttons, and containment matching cannot tell the two apart. Decide this when you reach for the component, not from a finding.

patterns.summary: The parts a Drawer is made of.
patterns.use: Editing something already on screen, or a flow a Dialog would cramp.

patterns.summary: The parts a Popover is made of.
patterns.use: Anchored, non-modal, interactive content.

patterns.summary: The parts a Menu is made of.
patterns.use: Commands, navigation destinations and in-menu settings.

patterns.summary: The parts a Select is made of.
patterns.use: Choosing one predefined value.

patterns.summary: The parts a Combobox is made of.
patterns.use: A value chosen from a filterable list.

patterns.summary: The parts an Autocomplete is made of.
patterns.use: Free-form text with suggestions.

patterns.summary: The parts a Tabs is made of.
patterns.use: Peer views of one subject.
instead_of: Tabs standing in for hierarchy — peers belong in tabs, depth belongs in navigation

patterns.summary: The parts an Accordion is made of.
patterns.use: Several independently expandable sections.
instead_of: An Accordion holding a single section — that is Collapsible

patterns.summary: The parts a NavigationMenu is made of.
patterns.use: Site or app navigation with rich panels.

patterns.summary: A labelled control with its description and validation message.
patterns.use: Any input that needs more than a placeholder.
instead_of: A Stack holding a <label> above an Input, with the error message conditionally rendered beside it — Field owns the association, the aria wiring and the rhythm
A placeholder standing in for a label

patterns.summary: A roving-focus bar of actions, grouped and separated.
patterns.use: An action bar with more than a couple of controls, especially one with groups.
instead_of: A Stack of Buttons with a Separator between the groups — it looks the same and has no roving focus, so every control is a tab stop
patterns.note: A plain `Button` inside a `Toolbar` is the same defect one level down: it drops out of the roving-focus order. Use `ToolbarButton`.

patterns.summary: Two or three actions sitting together, primary last.
patterns.use: The foot of a dialog, the end of a form, the corner of a header.
instead_of: A div with hand-set margins between the buttons
patterns.note: Documentation, not a check — `Stack(Button,Button)` is a true description of an action bar and matches half of any codebase. There is no canonical: two buttons in a Stack with a gap is already the whole implementation. Reach for `toolbar` instead once there are groups or more than about four controls.

patterns.summary: Transient messages raised from anywhere in the app.
patterns.use: Anything reporting the result of an action the user has already left behind.
instead_of: A hand-managed array of messages in component state, rendered into a fixed-position Stack — the manager already owns queueing, timing, focus and dismissal
An inline error rendered where the button was
patterns.note: Mount `ToastProvider` once at the app root and raise from `useToastManager()`. There is nothing to compose, which is why this entry carries no signature.

patterns.summary: Secondary actions on a thing — rename, duplicate, delete.
patterns.use: A row, card or header with more actions than deserve their own button.
instead_of: Three secondary Buttons sitting in the header, competing with the one action that matters

patterns.summary: Screen title, optional description, and a trailing action cluster.
patterns.use: The top of any screen or pane.
instead_of: An ad-hoc row rebuilt per screen, each with its own heading level and spacing
patterns.note: Archer ships no header component and no text component — the heading is a semantic element carrying a `type-style`. Extract one implementation the first time a second screen needs it, then fill in `import` and `canonical` here so the engine stops reporting the rebuilds and starts naming the answer.

patterns.summary: What a list, table or panel shows when it holds nothing yet.
patterns.use: Any collection that can legitimately be empty.
instead_of: A bare 'No results' string where the rows would be
A spinner that never resolves because there is nothing to load
patterns.note: Not shipped. Extract it once two exist and fill in `import`/`canonical`.

patterns.summary: A panel of properties beside a main region.
patterns.use: Inspecting or editing the selected thing without leaving the view.
instead_of: One-off panel layouts, each with its own width, padding and section rhythm
patterns.note: Not shipped. `Stack` plus `Separator` plus `Field` is the raw material; extract the composition once two exist.

patterns.summary: Rows that open a further screen, rather than a wall of controls.
patterns.use: Settings more than one level deep.
instead_of: One long panel showing every control at once
A Select that swaps the pane beneath it
patterns.note: Not shipped, and worth building rather than flattening: depth beats breadth, and a leaf screen that shows only what is actually set is far shorter than the panel it replaces.
